meta.generator: vectors/dweb-verify (cargo run --release -- cases; generate and check include it)
meta.design: docs/design/0009-dweb-verification.md, Tests first: the adversarial vectors, as checks on single pieces
meta.source: design: each case's expect is the design's, written by hand in src/cases/; the generator lays out and signs the bytes and checks each case's shape

oracles.ant: Ant v0.5.71 (910452d): ant_crypto::cac_valid and soc_valid on the same bytes
oracles.native: freedom-ipfs e7dcc6f, the commit freedom-ipfsd pins: freedom_ipfs_core::verify_block, parse_car_v1 (its whole-buffer CAR parser, which checks no block) and freedom_ipfs_namesys::verify_ipns_record on the same bytes. In this generator's graph, libp2p-identity also has its ecdsa and secp256k1 features (through Ant's libp2p), which freedom-ipfsd's doesn't: for an ECDSA key the generator's build checks the signature where freedom-ipfsd's fails to decode the key. Both refuse the case here

formats.bytes: {base64}; or, for bytes past 64 KiB, {parts, length, sha256}: the parts concatenated, each {base64}, {zeros: n} or {repeat: {base64, count}}
formats.expect: {ok: {…}} with what the check yields, or {fail: code}. Codes, as 0009's Failures names them: verification_failed (the bytes aren't what their address, CID or signature commits to, or the framing around them is broken), unverifiable (authentic, or possibly so, but outside what the core checks: a single-owner chunk off the feed path, an encrypted reference, an unsupported hash, structure past the decoders' caps), malformed (authentic content that can't be decoded or is inconsistent)
formats.oracles: ant and native record the pinned nodes' own verdict on the same bytes. Where it differs from expect, the case names the deviation (0009, Parity)
formats.swarm_chunks: a piece fetched as /chunks/<address> where the walk needs a content-addressed chunk (a root, a manifest node, an intermediate chunk, or a leaf's fallback): address, wire, expect {ok: {span_hex, payload_length}} or {fail}. span_hex is the wire's 8-byte span as sent (little-endian, the level byte included)
formats.swarm_feed_updates: a piece fetched as /chunks/<address> where the walk computed a feed update's address: owner, topic, index, address (keccak256(keccak256(topic ‖ u64_be(index)) ‖ owner)), wire, expect {ok: {version: v1, timestamp, reference}} or {ok: {version: v2, root, span_hex, payload_length}}, or {fail}
formats.swarm_leaves: a leaf in a /bytes stream: address (as its parent names it), logical_length (from the parent's geometry), streamed (the stream's bytes for it), chunk (the wire /chunks/<address> answers, read only when the streamed bytes don't hash to the address), expect {ok: {fallback}} or {fail, fallback}; fallback says whether /chunks was read
formats.ipfs_blocks: a block as a CAR section or a raw block brings it: cid, block, expect {ok: {codec}} or {fail}
formats.ipfs_dag_pb: a block that passed its CID, decoded as dag-pb: cid, block, expect {ok: {links: [{hash, name, tsize}], data}} or {fail}; data is the Data field's bytes or null
formats.ipfs_unixfs: a dag-pb node's Data decoded as UnixFS, checked against its links where it is a file: cid, block, expect {ok: {type, filesize, blocksizes, data_length}} or {fail}
formats.ipfs_hamt: a name's lookup in dweb-verify.json's HAMT (ipfs.directories, hamt-v1; its shards are in ipfs.blocks): root, name, hash_bits (the first 64 bits of MurmurHash3 x64 128 of the name, seed 0, big-endian; a byte per level), levels (per shard: depth, bucket, and the link named by the bucket's two uppercase hex digits, alone for a sub-shard or followed by the name for an entry, or null), expect {ok: {cid}} or {absent: true}. The generator checks every name against Kubo's own layout
formats.ipfs_car: a CAR body: car, expect {ok: {sections: [cid]}} when it reads to its end at a section boundary; {fail, after: k}, k the sections read whole before the failure; or {ended: {after: k}} when the stream ends inside a section, an early end the walk takes as a piece failure. Whether the walk then has what it needs is the walk's question, not the reader's
formats.ipns_records: an IPNS record as /ipns/<name>?format=ipns-record answers it: name, record, now (unix seconds), expect {ok: {value, sequence, validity, ttl_ns}} or {fail}
